rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis proposes high-temperature tensile and fracture toughness tests under plasma-facing conditions, whereas the paper used room-temperature compression, indentation plastometry up to 500 °C, and scratch testing. This is a different kind of study (mechanical testing vs. indentation/scratch) and a different temperature regime.
rationale.condition_agreement: The hypothesis specifies high temperatures (≥1000 °C) and plasma-facing conditions, while the paper tested from room temperature to 500 °C in air using compression, indentation, and scratch methods. The regimes are entirely different.
rationale.mechanism_agreement: The hypothesis invokes severe lattice distortion activating multiple slip systems and lowering the DBTT, while the paper attributes improved plasticity to Ti, V, Zr effects on valence-electron concentration, dislocation-core modification, grain-boundary cohesion, and crack propagation impedance. Both fall under the general class of dislocation-mediated plasticity, but the specific pathways differ substantially.
rationale.outcome_agreement: The hypothesis predicts higher plastic strain and fracture toughness under high-temperature plasma-facing conditions, while the paper measured higher strength, greater plastic strain, lower DBTT, less scratch damage, and higher scratch-based fracture toughness at room temperature to 500 °C. The predicted property and direction match, but the conditions and specific outcomes differ.
